observation.visible_scene: A night waterfront/harbor scene: a low lit building and a bridge on the left, moored sailboats and masts on the right, scattered streetlights, and a calm dark water surface in the foreground that mirrors the lights above. Multiple fireworks bursts illuminate the black sky just above the shoreline throughout the excerpt.
visible_changes: At the start a small white spherical burst of dots sits left-of-center; the shoreline buildings, boats and streetlights remain in fixed positions, indicating no evident camera pan.
Two small orange/red star-shaped bursts appear to the right of the white burst and persist for several frames.
The white burst enlarges and shifts toward green, becoming a broad green-and-white spherical burst of dots that expands in place at center.
Additional bursts appear and overlap at center, growing into a large green/white cloud-like spread of dots that dominates the middle of the frame.
Smaller red/orange bursts continue to pop to the right of the main green burst.
The central green burst gradually fades, its dots dimming and taking on purple/pink tones, leaving a sparse scatter of faint colored dots.
A green spherical burst on the right stays comparatively bright through the later frames while the left bursts fade.
Vertical white light streaks (rocket/fountain trails) near the right side of the sky are present in early frames and reappear/persist in later frames.
The water below shows mirrored reflections of each burst and of the vertical streaks; these reflections track the sky events and are not separate objects.
outside_clip_unknowns: The detonation moments that produced the bursts before t=0 and after the last frame are not shown.
Whether the fireworks sequence continues, pauses, or ends after the excerpt is unknown.
The launch points or any operator/equipment are not visible.
uncertain_details: Camera motion is uncertain; the static background suggests a fixed viewpoint, but slight drift cannot be ruled out.
The vertical streaks could be ascending/descending firework trails or persistent ground-mounted lights; their exact nature is not determinable from the frames.
Color shifts in the fading bursts may partly reflect exposure/decay rather than a change in the firework's intended color.
